ex.en: A timely snow promises a good harvest.
ex.zh: 瑞雪兆豐年。

ex.en: Thank you for your timely reply.
ex.zh: 謝謝你及時回覆。

ex.en: We need timely information to make decisions.
ex.zh: 我們需要及時的資訊來做決定。

timely.en: happening at just the right moment

ex.en: Is the timer running?
ex.zh: 計時器有在跑嗎？

ex.en: The button battery in the PC's internal timer has gone flat.
ex.zh: 電腦內部計時器的鈕扣電池沒電了。

ex.en: Set the timer for ten minutes.
ex.zh: 把計時器設定為十分鐘。

timer.en: a device that measures time or switches something on or off after a set period

ex.en: How many tiles do you need?
ex.zh: 你需要幾塊磁磚？

ex.en: The bathroom floor is covered with white tiles.
ex.zh: 浴室地板鋪著白色磁磚。

tile.en: a flat square piece of hard material used to cover floors, walls or roofs

ex.en: We had the kitchen floor tiled last month.
ex.zh: 我們上個月請人把廚房地板鋪了磁磚。

ex.en: They tiled the walls in blue.
ex.zh: 他們用藍色磁磚貼牆。

tile.en: to cover a floor or wall with flat square pieces of hard material

ex.en: Now all you have to do is tighten the screw, and Bob's your uncle.
ex.zh: 現在你只要把螺絲鎖緊就大功告成了。

ex.en: Please tighten your seat belt.
ex.zh: 請繫緊安全帶。

tighten.en: to become firmer or less loose, or to make something so

tighten.zh: 加強、收緊（規定、控制）；tighten one's belt 節省開支

ex.en: Critics are coming down hard on tightened economic restrictions.
ex.zh: 收緊經濟管制的措施遭到批評者猛烈抨擊。

ex.en: Small businesses will have to tighten their belts to survive.
ex.zh: 小型企業必須勒緊褲帶才能生存。

ex.en: The airport has tightened security.
ex.zh: 機場加強了安檢。

tighten.en: to make rules or controls stricter, or to spend less money

ex.en: Our service offers three pricing tiers.
ex.zh: 我們的服務提供三種價格方案等級。

ex.en: Customers in the top tier get free shipping.
ex.zh: 最高等級的會員享有免運費。

tier.en: one of several levels in a system

ex.en: The wedding cake had three tiers.
ex.zh: 那個結婚蛋糕有三層。

ex.en: The stadium has two tiers of seats.
ex.zh: 這座體育場有上下兩層座位。

tier.en: one of several rows or layers placed above each other

ex.en: There is a shortage of good construction timber right now.
ex.zh: 目前缺乏優質的建築用木材。

ex.en: The house is built of timber.
ex.zh: 這棟房子是木造的。

timber.en: wood that is used for building or making things

ex.en: The tide is coming in.
ex.zh: 正在漲潮。

ex.en: You can walk to the island at low tide.
ex.zh: 退潮時可以走路到那座島。

tide.en: the regular rising and falling of the sea

ex.en: The tide of public opinion is turning.
ex.zh: 輿論風向正在轉變。

ex.en: It's hard to swim against the tide.
ex.zh: 要逆勢而行很難。

tide.en: the general direction in which opinions or events are moving

tide.zh: tide (sb) over：幫（某人）度過難關、撐過一段時間

ex.en: Can you lend me $100 to tide me over?
ex.zh: 你能借我一百塊，讓我撐過這陣子嗎？

ex.en: This snack will tide you over until dinner.
ex.zh: 這份點心可以讓你撐到晚餐。

tide.en: to help someone get through a difficult period, especially with money

ex.en: Please tick the box if you want to receive our newsletter.
ex.zh: 如果想收到我們的電子報，請勾選此方塊。

ex.en: Tick all the options that apply.
ex.zh: 勾選所有符合的選項。

tick.en: to mark a small sign next to an item to show it is correct or chosen

ex.en: Put a tick next to the correct answer.
ex.zh: 在正確答案旁邊打勾。

ex.en: I put a tick next to each completed task.
ex.zh: 我在每一項完成的工作旁邊打了勾。

tick.en: a small mark that shows something is correct or has been chosen

ex.en: The only sound to be heard was the ticking of the clock.
ex.zh: 唯一聽得到的聲音是時鐘的滴答聲。

ex.en: Time ticks by more slowly around a black hole.
ex.zh: 黑洞附近的時間流逝得比較慢。

tick.en: to make a regular short sound like a clock, or to pass slowly

tick.zh: what makes (sb/sth) tick：（某人）的想法動機；（某物）的運作原理

ex.en: I like to take things apart to see what makes them tick.
ex.zh: 我喜歡把東西拆開，看看它們是怎麼運作的。

ex.en: I'd love to know what makes him tick.
ex.zh: 我很想知道他腦子裡在想什麼。

tick.en: the reasons why a person behaves as they do, or how a thing works

ex.en: I don't have time to cook tonight.
ex.zh: 我今晚沒時間煮飯。

ex.en: Time flies when you're busy.
ex.zh: 忙的時候時間過得特別快。

time.en: what is measured in minutes, hours and days

time.zh: 時刻、時候（幾點；該…的時候）

ex.en: It's time for you to buy a new car.
ex.zh: 你該買一輛新車了。

ex.en: What time is it?
ex.zh: 現在幾點？

time.en: a particular moment or point in the day or a suitable moment for something

ex.en: I've been to Japan three times.
ex.zh: 我去過日本三次。

ex.en: This is my first time here.
ex.zh: 這是我第一次來這裡。

time.en: an occasion when something happens or is done

ex.en: The deer is three times as heavy as Jane.
ex.zh: 那隻鹿是簡的三倍重。

ex.en: This river is three times longer than that one.
ex.zh: 這條河是那條河的三倍長。

time.en: used to show how many more or less of something there is by comparison

ex.en: Please be on time for the meeting.
ex.zh: 開會請準時。

ex.en: We arrived just in time for the show.
ex.zh: 我們剛好及時趕上表演。

time.en: at the planned moment, or early enough

ex.en: What is the title of your new book?
ex.zh: 你新書的書名是什麼？

ex.en: What is the title of the book?
ex.zh: 這本書的書名是什麼？

ex.en: The novel takes its title from the Bible.
ex.zh: 這本小說的書名出自《聖經》。

title.en: the name of a book, film, song or piece of writing

ex.en: What is your job title at the company?
ex.zh: 你在公司的職稱是什麼？

ex.en: She was given the title of senior manager.
ex.zh: 她被授予資深經理的頭銜。

title.en: a word or name that shows a person's rank or job

ex.en: The team won the national title last year.
ex.zh: 這支隊伍去年拿下全國冠軍。

ex.en: He has held the world title for three years.
ex.zh: 他已經保持世界冠軍頭銜三年了。

title.en: the position of being the winner of a sports competition

ex.en: The rear tire of my bicycle is flat.
ex.zh: 我腳踏車的後輪沒氣了。

ex.en: Take a look at these tires.
ex.zh: 看看這些輪胎。

ex.en: I had a flat tire on the way to work.
ex.zh: 我上班途中爆胎了。

tire.en: a thick rubber ring around a wheel of a vehicle

ex.en: You work too hard these days. Aren't you tired?
ex.zh: 你這幾天工作太賣力了，不累嗎？

ex.en: Long meetings really tire me out.
ex.zh: 冗長的會議真的讓我筋疲力盡。

tire.en: to make someone feel that they need rest, or to need rest

tire.zh: be tired of / tire of：厭倦

ex.en: I'm tired of eating fast food every day.
ex.zh: 我厭倦了每天吃速食。

ex.en: She never tires of hearing that song.
ex.zh: 那首歌她百聽不厭。

tire.en: to become bored with or annoyed by something

ex.en: This shirt doesn't go with that tie at all.
ex.zh: 這件襯衫跟那條領帶一點都不搭。

ex.en: Can you show me how to tie a tie?
ex.zh: 你能教我怎麼打領帶嗎？

tie.en: a long narrow piece of cloth worn around the neck under a shirt collar

ex.en: The boat was tied with a short line.
ex.zh: 船用一條短繩綁著。

ex.en: She wore a ribbon tied around her hair.
ex.zh: 她頭髮上綁了一條緞帶。

tie.en: to fasten something using string, rope or similar

ex.en: The two nations have strong trade ties.
ex.zh: 這兩國有密切的貿易關係。

ex.en: The company has close ties with local universities.
ex.zh: 這家公司和本地大學關係密切。

tie.en: a connection between people, groups or countries

ex.en: The match ended in a tie.
ex.zh: 比賽以平手收場。

ex.en: The vote was a tie, so we voted again.
ex.zh: 投票結果同票，所以我們重新投票。

tie.en: a result in a game or contest where both sides have the same score

ex.en: We carried on the discussion till late at night.
ex.zh: 我們一直討論到深夜。

ex.en: I lived in the US from 2008 till 2011.
ex.zh: 我從 2008 年到 2011 年住在美國。

ex.en: Did you stay till the end of the concert?
ex.zh: 你一直待到演唱會結束嗎？

till.en: up to the time when something happens

ex.en: You never know what you can do till you try.
ex.zh: 不試試看，你永遠不知道自己能做什麼。

ex.en: Please wait here till I come back.
ex.zh: 請在這裡等我回來。

till.en: up to the time when something happens

ex.en: The cashier put the money in the till.
ex.zh: 收銀員把錢放進收銀機。

ex.en: There was only 500 dollars in the till.
ex.zh: 收銀機裡只有五百元。

till.en: a drawer or machine in a shop where money is kept

ex.en: He came from a tiny mountain town.
ex.zh: 他來自一個小山城。

ex.en: Add a tiny pinch of salt.
ex.zh: 加一小撮鹽。

ex.en: It's a tiny country that most people have never heard of.
ex.zh: 那是一個大多數人都沒聽過的小國。

ex.en: These shoes are too tight. They hurt.
ex.zh: 這雙鞋太緊了，穿了腳痛。

ex.en: These jeans are too tight for me.
ex.zh: 這件牛仔褲我穿太緊了。

tight.en: fitting closely, so that there is little or no space

ex.en: We are traveling on a tight budget.
ex.zh: 我們旅行的預算很緊。

ex.en: We are on a tight schedule this week.
ex.zh: 我們這週的行程很緊湊。

tight.en: with very little time or money available

ex.en: Hold on tight to the handrail.
ex.zh: 抓緊扶手。

ex.en: Close the lid tight after use.
ex.zh: 使用後請把蓋子蓋緊。

tight.en: firmly, so that something cannot move or come loose

ex.en: I think I'm gonna sneeze. Give me a tissue.
ex.zh: 我好像要打噴嚏了，給我一張面紙。

ex.en: Do you have a tissue? I have a runny nose.
ex.zh: 你有面紙嗎？我在流鼻水。

tissue.en: a thin soft piece of paper used for wiping your nose

ex.en: Human tissue is made up of cells.
ex.zh: 人體組織是由細胞構成的。

ex.en: The doctor removed a small piece of tissue for testing.
ex.zh: 醫生取了一小塊組織去檢驗。

tissue.en: a mass of cells that forms part of a living thing

ex.en: We do not accept tips.
ex.zh: 本店不收小費。

ex.en: We left a 15% tip for the waiter.
ex.zh: 我們給服務生 15% 的小費。

tip.en: a small extra amount of money given to someone for good service

ex.en: You'd better remember that tipping is necessary in the USA.
ex.zh: 你最好記住，在美國一定要給小費。

ex.en: There is no tipping culture in China.
ex.zh: 中國沒有給小費的文化。

tip.en: to give a small extra amount of money for good service

ex.en: I'll keep the tips you shared for improving my presentation skills.
ex.zh: 你分享的提升簡報技巧的建議，我會記下來。

ex.en: Here are some tips for learning English.
ex.zh: 以下是一些學英文的訣竅。

tip.en: a useful piece of advice or practical information

ex.en: It's on the tip of my tongue.
ex.zh: 話就在嘴邊，可是想不起來。

ex.en: The tip of the pencil broke.
ex.zh: 鉛筆的筆尖斷了。

tip.en: the narrow or pointed end of something

ex.en: I admit, I'm not the tidiest person in the world.
ex.zh: 我承認我不是世界上最愛整潔的人。

ex.en: Please keep your desk tidy.
ex.zh: 請保持桌面整齊。

tidy.en: arranged neatly, or liking to keep things in good order

ex.en: My room is a tip. I need to tidy it.
ex.zh: 我的房間亂七八糟，得整理一下。

ex.en: We will tidy up our room so that Mom is satisfied.
ex.zh: 我們會把房間整理好，讓媽媽滿意。

tidy.en: to make a place neat by putting things where they belong

ex.en: You must be tired after such a long trip.
ex.zh: 在這麼長程的旅途後你一定很累了。

ex.en: I'm so tired that I can't walk any longer.
ex.zh: 我累得走不動了。

ex.en: I went to bed early, for I was tired.
ex.zh: 我很早上床睡覺了，因為很累。

tired.en: feeling that you need to rest or sleep

ex.en: A mouse is a timid creature.
ex.zh: 老鼠是膽小的生物。

ex.en: He is a timid man.
ex.zh: 他是個膽小怕事的人。

ex.en: She is timid like a rabbit.
ex.zh: 她像兔子一樣膽小。

ex.en: If your children are being tiresome, you will feel time passing slowly.
ex.zh: 如果你的孩子很辛苦你覺得日子很漫長。

ex.en: Filling out the same form again and again is tiresome.
ex.zh: 一再重複填寫同一份表格實在令人厭煩。

tiresome.en: making you feel annoyed or bored

ex.en: New York and Taipei are in different time zones.
ex.zh: 紐約和台北在不同的時區。

ex.en: It's hard to schedule meetings across time zones.
ex.zh: 跨時區安排會議很不容易。

time zone.en: one of the areas of the world that use the same clock hours

ex.en: I'd like two one-way tickets from A to B.
ex.zh: 麻煩給我兩張從 A 到 B 的單程票。

ex.en: The concert ticket costs more than the cinema ticket.
ex.zh: 演唱會門票比電影票貴。

ex.en: Can I pick my ticket up at the airport?
ex.zh: 我可以在機場取票嗎？

ticket.en: a piece of paper or card that lets you travel or enter a place

ex.en: I got a parking ticket yesterday.
ex.zh: 我昨天被開了一張違規停車罰單。

ex.en: He got a speeding ticket on the highway.
ex.zh: 他在高速公路上被開了超速罰單。

ticket.en: an official paper that tells a person to pay money for breaking a traffic rule

ex.en: Is there a timetable?
ex.zh: 有時刻表嗎？

ex.en: According to the timetable, the next train leaves at 9:15.
ex.zh: 根據時刻表，下一班火車 9 點 15 分開。

timetable.en: a list showing the times when buses, trains or classes are planned

ex.en: What's the timeline for the new website?
ex.zh: 新網站的時程是怎麼安排的？

ex.en: The timeline is too tight to finish everything.
ex.zh: 時程太緊了，沒辦法全部做完。

timeline.en: a plan showing when each part of a project should happen

ex.en: The old toys were made of tin.
ex.zh: 這些老玩具是用錫做的。

ex.en: Tin is a soft, silver-white metal.
ex.zh: 錫是一種柔軟的銀白色金屬。

ex.en: She opened a tin of tomatoes for the sauce.
ex.zh: 她開了一罐番茄來做醬汁。

ex.en: He keeps cookies in a metal tin.
ex.zh: 他把餅乾放在一個鐵罐裡。

ex.en: We brought a few tins of fish for the trip.
ex.zh: 我們帶了幾罐魚罐頭去旅行。

ex.en: Good timing is important when you tell a joke.
ex.zh: 講笑話時，抓對時機很重要。

ex.en: The timing of the meeting was not convenient for me.
ex.zh: 會議的時間對我來說不太方便。

ex.en: His timing was perfect, and he arrived just as dinner was served.
ex.zh: 他的時機抓得剛剛好，正好在上菜時抵達。

ex.en: She held the baby tightly in her arms.
ex.zh: 她把嬰兒緊緊抱在懷裡。

ex.en: Make sure the lid is tightly closed.
ex.zh: 請確定蓋子已經蓋緊。

ex.en: The bag was packed tightly with clothes.
ex.zh: 袋子裡緊緊塞滿了衣服。

ex.en: We saw a tiger sleeping in the shade at the zoo.
ex.zh: 我們在動物園看到一隻老虎在樹蔭下睡覺。

ex.en: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family.
ex.zh: 老虎是貓科動物中體型最大的。

ex.en: Tim is a short form of the name Timothy.
ex.zh: 蒂姆是提摩西這個名字的簡稱。

ex.en: Tim practices the guitar for an hour every evening.
ex.zh: 蒂姆每天晚上練一個小時吉他。

ex.en: She tilted her head and listened carefully.
ex.zh: 她歪著頭仔細聆聽。

ex.en: Don't tilt the glass or the water will spill.
ex.zh: 別把杯子傾斜，不然水會灑出來。

ex.en: The old table tilts to one side because a leg is shorter.
ex.zh: 那張舊桌子因為有一隻腳比較短，所以會往一邊傾斜。

ex.en: The tower has a slight tilt to the left.
ex.zh: 這座塔略微向左傾斜。

ex.en: With a tilt of her hat, she greeted us.
ex.zh: 她把帽子輕輕一傾，向我們打了招呼。

ex.en: I've watched this movie three times already.
ex.zh: 這部電影我已經看過三次了。

ex.en: How many times do I have to tell you to clean your room?
ex.zh: 我到底要跟你說幾次才會去整理房間？

ex.en: This room is three times bigger than mine.
ex.zh: 這個房間比我的大三倍。

ex.en: Prices are twice as high here, sometimes four times higher.
ex.zh: 這裡的物價高出一倍，有時甚至高出三倍。

ex.en: We lived through some hard times together.
ex.zh: 我們一起度過了一些艱困的時期。

ex.en: Times have changed since my grandparents were young.
ex.zh: 自從我祖父母年輕的時候，時代已經變了。

ex.en: The tidal pool was full of tiny crabs.
ex.zh: 潮池裡有許多小螃蟹。

ex.en: Fishermen check the tidal chart before going out.
ex.zh: 漁夫出海前會查看潮汐表。

ex.en: The river is tidal for the last ten miles.
ex.zh: 這條河最後十英里會受潮汐影響。

ex.en: She tickled the baby's feet and he giggled.
ex.zh: 她搔寶寶的腳底，寶寶咯咯笑了起來。

ex.en: Stop tickling me, I can't stop laughing!
ex.zh: 別再搔我癢了，我笑個不停！

ex.en: The wool scarf tickles my neck.
ex.zh: 這條羊毛圍巾讓我的脖子癢癢的。

ex.en: My throat tickles whenever I breathe in the dust.
ex.zh: 我一吸到灰塵，喉嚨就癢癢的。

ex.en: I have a tickle in my throat and keep coughing.
ex.zh: 我喉嚨發癢，一直咳嗽。

ex.en: The feather gave her a little tickle on the nose.
ex.zh: 羽毛輕輕搔得她的鼻子癢癢的。

timeless.zh: 永恆的；不受時間影響的

ex.en: The song has a timeless beauty that people still love.
ex.zh: 這首歌有著永恆的美，人們至今仍喜愛。

ex.en: Her black dress is simple and timeless.
ex.zh: 她的黑色洋裝簡單又不退流行。

ex.en: The old village has a timeless charm.
ex.zh: 這座古老村莊有種歷久不衰的魅力。

ex.en: The frame of this bike is made of titanium.
ex.zh: 這輛腳踏車的車架是鈦製的。

ex.en: Titanium is strong, light, and does not rust easily.
ex.zh: 鈦又堅固又輕，而且不容易生鏽。

ex.en: He likes to tinker with old radios in his garage.
ex.zh: 他喜歡在車庫裡擺弄舊收音機。

ex.en: She tinkered with the recipe until it tasted perfect.
ex.zh: 她反覆調整食譜，直到味道完美為止。

ex.en: In the old story, a tinker came to the village to mend pots.
ex.zh: 在那則老故事裡，一位補鍋匠來到村子修理鍋子。

ex.en: The tinker traveled from town to town with his tools.
ex.zh: 那位補鍋匠帶著工具到處旅行。

ex.en: It was a long and tiring journey.
ex.zh: 那是一趟漫長又累人的旅程。

ex.en: Looking after three kids all day is tiring.
ex.zh: 整天照顧三個孩子很累人。

ex.en: Tiredness made it hard to focus at work.
ex.zh: 疲倦讓他很難專心工作。

ex.en: She felt a wave of tiredness after the long flight.
ex.zh: 長途飛行後，她感到一陣疲憊。

ex.en: We visited a Tibetan temple in the mountains.
ex.zh: 我們參觀了山裡的一座西藏寺廟。

ex.en: Tibetan tea is made with butter and salt.
ex.zh: 藏茶是用奶油和鹽調製的。

ex.en: The monk is a Tibetan who teaches meditation.
ex.zh: 這位僧人是教授冥想的藏人。

ex.en: She is learning Tibetan to read old books.
ex.zh: 她正在學藏語以便閱讀古書。

ex.en: The bathroom has a tiled floor that is easy to clean.
ex.zh: 浴室鋪著容易清洗的磁磚地板。

ex.en: They sat in a tiled courtyard under the shade.
ex.zh: 他們坐在鋪著磁磚的中庭樹蔭下。

ex.en: The tiller of the soil rises early in the morning.
ex.zh: 耕田的人一早就起床。

ex.en: Each tiller on the farm shared the harvest.
ex.zh: 農場裡的每位耕作者都分得一份收成。

ex.en: He held the tiller and steered the small boat toward the shore.
ex.zh: 他握著舵柄，把小船駛向岸邊。

ex.en: Push the tiller to the left to turn right.
ex.zh: 把舵柄推向左邊，船就會向右轉。

ex.en: She tiptoed past the sleeping baby.
ex.zh: 她踮著腳尖走過熟睡的嬰兒身邊。

ex.en: We tiptoed down the stairs so we wouldn't wake our parents.
ex.zh: 我們踮著腳下樓，以免吵醒爸媽。

ex.en: The little girl stood on tiptoe to reach the shelf.
ex.zh: 小女孩踮起腳尖去拿架子上的東西。

ex.en: I had to stand on tiptoe to see over the crowd.
ex.zh: 我得踮起腳尖才能看到人群後面。

ex.en: The sky had a pink tinge at sunset.
ex.zh: 日落時天空帶著一抹粉紅。

ex.en: There was a tinge of sadness in his voice.
ex.zh: 他的聲音裡帶著一絲悲傷。

ex.en: Autumn began to tinge the leaves with red.
ex.zh: 秋天開始讓樹葉染上紅色。

ex.en: Her smile was tinged with regret.
ex.zh: 她的笑容裡帶著些許遺憾。

ex.en: She wore black tights under her skirt.
ex.zh: 她在裙子裡面穿了黑色褲襪。

ex.en: The dancers put on tights before the rehearsal.
ex.zh: 舞者在排練前穿上緊身褲。

ex.en: Wait here til I get back from the store.
ex.zh: 在這裡等，等我從店裡回來。

ex.en: She kept working til the sun went down.
ex.zh: 她一直工作到太陽下山。

ex.en: We had tinned soup and bread for lunch.
ex.zh: 我們午餐吃了罐頭湯和麵包。

ex.en: Tinned tomatoes are cheaper than fresh ones in winter.
ex.zh: 冬天罐裝番茄比新鮮的便宜。

ex.en: My fingers began to tingle in the cold.
ex.zh: 我的手指在寒冷中開始刺痛發麻。

ex.en: Her skin tingled after she stepped out of the hot shower.
ex.zh: 她走出熱水澡後，皮膚微微發麻。

ex.en: I felt a tingle of excitement as the concert began.
ex.zh: 演唱會開始時，我感到一陣興奮的顫慄。

ex.en: The mint gum leaves a cool tingle in your mouth.
ex.zh: 薄荷口香糖讓嘴裡留下清涼的刺麻感。

tightening.zh: 拉緊；收緊（tighten 的現在分詞）

ex.en: He is tightening the screws on the chair.
ex.zh: 他正在鎖緊椅子上的螺絲。

ex.en: The bank is tightening its rules on loans.
ex.zh: 銀行正在收緊貸款的規定。

tireless.zh: 不知疲倦的；不屈不撓的

ex.en: The tireless nurse worked all night to care for the patients.
ex.zh: 那位不知疲倦的護理師整晚照顧病人。

ex.en: He is a tireless supporter of the local animal shelter.
ex.zh: 他是當地動物收容所不遺餘力的支持者。

ex.en: The sky had a pink tint at sunrise.
ex.zh: 日出時，天空帶著淡淡的粉紅色調。

ex.en: The glasses have a slight blue tint.
ex.zh: 這副眼鏡帶有淡淡的藍色。

ex.en: She wants to tint her hair a light brown.
ex.zh: 她想把頭髮染成淺棕色。

ex.en: They tint the car windows to keep the sun out.
ex.zh: 他們給車窗貼上深色隔熱膜來擋太陽。

ex.en: She tied her shoes before the race.
ex.zh: 她在比賽前綁好了鞋帶。

ex.en: He tied the boat to the dock with a thick rope.
ex.zh: 他用粗繩把船綁在碼頭上。

ex.en: The two teams tied at three goals each.
ex.zh: 兩隊各進三球，打成平手。

ex.en: We tied for second place in the contest.
ex.zh: 我們在比賽中並列第二名。

ex.en: The clock was ticking loudly in the quiet room.
ex.zh: 安靜的房間裡，時鐘滴答響得很大聲。

ex.en: She is ticking off the items on her shopping list.
ex.zh: 她正在購物清單上逐項打勾。

ex.en: The ticking of the clock kept me awake all night.
ex.zh: 時鐘的滴答聲讓我整晚睡不著。

ex.en: All I could hear was the ticking from the old watch.
ex.zh: 我只聽得到那隻舊手錶的滴答聲。

ex.en: He has a nervous tic that makes his eye blink often.
ex.zh: 他有個神經性的抽動，讓他的眼睛常常眨動。

ex.en: The little girl's tic gets worse when she is tired.
ex.zh: 那個小女孩累的時候，抽動會更嚴重。

ex.en: In Greek myths, the Titans were giants who ruled before the gods.
ex.zh: 在希臘神話中，泰坦是比眾神更早統治世界的巨人。

ex.en: He is a titan of the technology industry.
ex.zh: 他是科技業的巨擘。

ex.en: Loud concerts can cause tinnitus.
ex.zh: 大聲的演唱會可能造成耳鳴。

ex.en: He sees a doctor because of his constant tinnitus.
ex.zh: 他因為持續耳鳴而去看醫生。

ex.en: Tibet is known for its high mountains.
ex.zh: 西藏以高聳的山脈聞名。

ex.en: Many travelers dream of visiting the plateau of Tibet.
ex.zh: 許多旅人夢想造訪西藏高原。

ex.en: She shared a fun tidbit about the history of the building.
ex.zh: 她分享了一則有關這棟建築歷史的有趣小知識。

ex.en: Here's a tidbit of news you might like to hear.
ex.zh: 這裡有一則你可能想聽的小消息。

ex.en: The cat was given a tidbit of chicken.
ex.zh: 貓咪得到了一小塊雞肉。

ex.en: The waiter brought us a tidbit to try before the main dish.
ex.zh: 服務生在主菜前端來一小份美食讓我們嚐嚐。

ex.en: The car has tinted windows that block the sun.
ex.zh: 這輛車的窗戶貼了隔熱色膜，能擋住陽光。

ex.en: She wore tinted glasses on the bright day.
ex.zh: 那天陽光很強，她戴了有色眼鏡。

ex.en: He launched into a tirade about the noisy neighbors.
ex.zh: 他開始對吵鬧的鄰居長篇大論地怒罵。

ex.en: The coach's angry tirade left the players silent.
ex.zh: 教練憤怒的長篇斥責讓球員們鴉雀無聲。

ex.en: The nurses worked tirelessly through the night.
ex.zh: 護理師們整夜不知疲倦地工作。

ex.en: She tirelessly practiced the piano until she got it right.
ex.zh: 她不知疲倦地練習鋼琴，直到彈對為止。

tiananmen.zh: 天安門（北京的城樓與廣場）

ex.en: Tiananmen is a famous gate and square in the center of Beijing.
ex.zh: 天安門是北京市中心著名的城樓與廣場。

ex.en: Many tourists visit Tiananmen Square every day.
ex.zh: 每天有許多遊客造訪天安門廣場。

ex.en: She felt a tightness in her chest before the big exam.
ex.zh: 大考前她感到胸口一陣緊繃。

ex.en: The tightness of the jeans made it hard to sit down.
ex.zh: 這條牛仔褲太緊，讓人很難坐下。

ex.en: The acrobat walked across the tightrope with a long pole.
ex.zh: 特技演員拿著長桿走過鋼索。

ex.en: Managing two jobs is like walking a tightrope.
ex.zh: 同時應付兩份工作就像走鋼索一樣。

ex.en: The two teams fought a titanic battle for the title.
ex.zh: 兩支球隊為了冠軍展開一場激烈的巨大對決。

ex.en: Moving the old bridge was a titanic task.
ex.zh: 移動那座舊橋是一項極其艱鉅的工程。

ex.en: The Titanic sank in the North Atlantic in 1912.
ex.zh: 鐵達尼號於 1912 年在北大西洋沉沒。

ex.en: We watched a documentary about the Titanic.
ex.zh: 我們看了一部關於鐵達尼號的紀錄片。

ex.en: The singer has a warm, rich timbre.
ex.zh: 這位歌手的音色溫暖而豐厚。

ex.en: A violin and a flute have different timbres.
ex.zh: 小提琴和長笛的音色不同。

ex.en: The stock ticker at the bottom of the screen showed prices.
ex.zh: 螢幕下方的股市行情跑馬燈顯示著股價。

ex.en: Traders watched the ticker closely all morning.
ex.zh: 交易員整個早上都緊盯著行情顯示器。

ex.en: The doctor said his ticker is in good shape.
ex.zh: 醫生說他的心臟狀況良好。

ex.en: Climbing stairs is good for your ticker.
ex.zh: 爬樓梯對你的心臟有益。

tithe.zh: 什一稅；十分之一的捐獻

ex.en: Farmers once paid a tithe to the church.
ex.zh: 農民過去要向教會繳納什一稅。

ex.en: She gave a tithe of her income every month.
ex.zh: 她每個月捐出收入的十分之一。

tithe.zh: 課什一稅；捐出十分之一收入

ex.en: Many members tithe regularly to their church.
ex.zh: 許多成員定期向教會奉獻十分之一的收入。

ex.en: He tithes a part of his salary each year.
ex.zh: 他每年把部分薪水奉獻出去。

ex.en: The runner broke his tibia during the match.
ex.zh: 那位跑者在比賽中摔斷了脛骨。

ex.en: The tibia is the larger bone in the lower leg.
ex.zh: 脛骨是小腿中較粗的那根骨頭。
